incoming.name: Stephen of England
incoming.section: Recognises Henry as his heir and dies
incoming.excerpt: The Anglo-Saxon Chronicle (the Peterborough Chronicle, second continuation) provides a moving and succinct appraisal of Stephen's reign:

incoming.name: The Anarchy
incoming.excerpt: The Peterborough Chronicle offers an eye-witness account of the civil war and its suffering.

outgoing.name: Abbot
outgoing.excerpt: It also covers ecclesiastical scandals, such as the abbot of Glastonbury bringing in mercenaries to control his religious house.

outgoing.name: Ancient Rome
outgoing.excerpt: Each chronicle began with the Creation, went through Biblical and Roman history, then continued to the present.

outgoing.name: Denmark
outgoing.excerpt: The first continuation records the Conquest, the incursion of Sweyn of Denmark, and rumors of other turbulence about the throne.

outgoing.name: Henry I of England
outgoing.excerpt: Henry I died in 1135, and Stephen and Matilda both had a claim to the throne.

outgoing.name: Stephen of England
outgoing.excerpt: The second continuation runs from 1132–1154 and includes the reign of King Stephen.

outgoing.name: The Anarchy
outgoing.excerpt: The second, or final, continuation is remarkable for being in one authorial voice, and it relates the events of The Anarchy in England.

outgoing.name: Archbishop of Canterbury
outgoing.excerpt: …was then Chancellor of Oxford University as well as Archbishop of Canterbury, on June 28, 1639.

outgoing.name: Jesus
outgoing.excerpt: Common peasants, the monk says, thought that Jesus slept and that God had turned his face away…
